A 9.2-in gun barrel display. Nothing too special about it, but it is worth a quick look.
A historic Australian Army site, with well preserved barracks and artillery with views of Sydney Harbour. Additionally, tours of underground tunnels are available on weekends.

Small beach, which has a small waterfall off a rock when rainy. The water here is unusually shallow as well, and looks more a tropical paradise rather than metropolitan Sydney. Not too hard to get to, but parking can become a problem.
A free display of all the antiques and items that were used during quarantine, including an old stove.
Features a historic World War II site that was put in place to prevent a Japanese invasion. However, it was never used and now it is a tourist spot.
North Head to Manly Trail, Manly

A harbour facing lookout, facing the Sydney skyline, including the harbour bridge, the Sydney Opera House, and the Sydney Eye. You might see some of the harbour islands although they may be obstructed by the trees.
A former hospital used to treat the infected when the quarantine station was in use. The hospital displays some of the early 19- and 20th-century medical tools.
Another one of Sydney Harbour's many small forts, built to prevent a WWII attack from the Japanese. You'll also have some impressive harbour views from the hill.

This is a swimming spot in Sydney Harbour. It is a fairly average beach, but has an interesting westerly outlook which allows you see the sun setting over the bay, which is very unusual in Sydney, where looking over the water usually…
You'd think that this is just your ordinary wharf, but there's some historic artwork here, depicting the styles of the early 20th century.
A difficult to access beach, but do-able from Collins Beach. It was where ships used to unload provisions for the Quarantine Station but now it can only be accessed by a private boat or by foot.
North Head to Manly trail, Manly
A cemetery for the third class passengers from the quarantined ships quarantining at the North Head Quarantine Station.
A bike path, but there's more people who walk this track.

A popular spot if you're a meatlover.
